clue.text: Cleaners put off by public conveniences

parts.note: to put someone off doing something is to deter them
GENTS is the British name for a men's public lavatory

explanation.surface: Someone is repelled from using public toilets by the cleaning staff or the cleaning fluids.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cleaners' reads as people who clean, but it means cleaning products. GENTS is the everyday British sign for a men's public toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Detergents are washing agents, substances used to clean things.

definitions.meaning: the organs of hearing take in sound
the grain-bearing heads of cereal plants such as wheat

explanation.surface: Some people or plants take in sound wheat that is healthy and good to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like an adjective describing the wheat, but it belongs with the first definition as the noise that hearing organs take in.
explanation.definitionFit: Ears hear noise, and an ear of wheat is the spike holding the grain, so both senses fit.

parts.note: suggests an aristocratic infant, but means a young bird hatched in a nest built high on a cliff

explanation.surface: A small child born into the nobility.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high birth' suggests noble rank; it is literal, since this young bird is born in an eyrie high on a crag.
explanation.definitionFit: A young eagle is hatched in an eyrie, a nest built at great height.

parts.note: suggests a soldier being dismissed from service, but means the firing of weapons by troops

explanation.surface: A soldier is being dismissed from military service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discharge' reads as dismissal; here it is the discharging of guns.
explanation.definitionFit: The firing of rifles and artillery is a discharge of weapons, something an army produces.

indicators.note: the word for love goes on the outside, wrapping round the letter A

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, NIL

explanation.surface: Someone's affection is safe only on the surface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outwardly' signals that NIL sits on the outside of A, giving N-A-IL.
explanation.definitionFit: To fasten something firmly in place, to secure it, you can hammer a metal pin through it.

parts.note: suggests someone snipping inside a crease of paper or cloth, but means a man clipping fleeces in a sheep pen

explanation.surface: A man trims something within a crease or folded edge.
explanation.walkthrough: A fold is also an enclosure for sheep, where wool is clipped.
explanation.definitionFit: A man who clips the wool from sheep works in a pen, the fold.

parts.note: merits or virtues, but also the movable rails that switch trains between tracks, if they are well made

explanation.surface: Someone lists the merits of a rail network.
explanation.walkthrough: On a railway, points are the switches that move trains from one track to another; well-working ones would be good ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Merits or strengths are someone's assets, and railway switches are called points.

clue.text: They accommodate those who don't wish to move when they retire

definitions.text: They accommodate those who don't wish to move when they retire

parts.words: They accommodate those who don't wish to move when they retire
parts.note: suggests housing for pensioners, but means one-room flats where a person sleeps and sits without moving rooms when going to bed

explanation.surface: Homes for people who want to stay put after giving up work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retire' means going to bed, not leaving work: in a one-room British flat you need not move from the sitting area to sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-room rented flat in Britain combines living and sleeping space in a single room.

clue.text: It took at least two days to build, possibly more

definitions.text: It took at least two days to build, possibly more

parts.words: It took at least two days to build, possibly more
parts.note: plays on the proverb that a famous ancient city was not built in a day

explanation.surface: A construction project that lasted two days or longer.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb says this city 'wasn't built in a day', so it took at least two.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb about patience says the Italian capital was not built in a day.

indicators.note: a derailed train has gone off its rails, so these letters are thrown into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A train comes off the tracks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being derailed' rearranges the letters of TRAIN BEING.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigantine is a two-masted sailing vessel, a kind of ship.

clue.text: Remarks we're not supposed to hear when the team comes in

definitions.text: Remarks we're not supposed to hear

indicators.note: the team arrives inside the word for when, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as he arrived'
a side is a team in sport

explanation.surface: Things the audience should not overhear are said as the players enter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes in' puts SIDE inside AS. On stage, an aside is spoken to the audience and supposedly unheard by the other characters.
explanation.definitionFit: Stage whispers are lines the other characters supposedly cannot hear.

clue.text: They must have been given credit for something

definitions.text: They must have been given credit for something

parts.words: They must have been given credit for something
parts.note: suggests people praised for an achievement, but means people who borrowed and owe money

explanation.surface: People who deserve recognition for some achievement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'credit' reads as praise; here it is a loan.
explanation.definitionFit: People who owe money have been lent it on credit.

parts.note: the late are the deceased, dead
punctual means on time

explanation.surface: A series of questions about whether someone is running late or on time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Late' means deceased, not delayed.
explanation.definitionFit: Arriving at precisely the appointed moment is being exactly prompt.

clue.text: Harmonious music for the hairdresser's ball?

parts.note: a men's hairdresser is a barber
a hop is an informal dance

explanation.surface: Asking what music suits a dance held by a hairdresser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ball' means a dance, not a sphere. The style is close-harmony singing, often by male quartets.
explanation.definitionFit: Close-harmony unaccompanied vocal music, typically sung by four men, takes its name from a men's hairdressing shop.

clue.text: Fire about fifty for being lax

indicators.note: the word for fire goes round the letter for fifty

parts.note: to fire someone is to sack them
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A boss dismisses about fifty workers for being careless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts SACK round L.
explanation.definitionFit: Being slack means being careless or loose, without proper tension or rigour.

clue.text: US city editor breaks down on junction

indicators.note: the word editor collapses and its letters are reassembled in another order

parts.note: a T-junction is a road junction shaped like the letter T

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor in an American city has a breakdown at a road junction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks down' rearranges EDITOR into DETROI; 'on' puts T after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Detroit is a large city in Michigan, famous for car making.

clue.text: Fellow holds me up showing bad spirit

indicators.note: the word for fellow contains the other piece, holding it inside

parts.note: a don is a fellow of a university college

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word me is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man delays someone and shows a nasty attitude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns ME into EM, and 'holds' puts that inside DON.
explanation.definitionFit: A demon is an evil supernatural being, a malevolent spirit.

clue.text: The Spanish return red wine, perhaps

parts.note: el is Spanish for the

indicators.note: the word red comes back, read from right to left

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The Spaniards send back the red wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' reverses RED to DER. 'perhaps' shows the definition is an example: this tree's berries and flowers make a homemade wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Elderberry and elderflower wines are made from this tree, so the tree name stands for a wine.

definitions.meaning: affected manners or appearances, as in putting on graces
tunes are things that are composed

explanation.surface: Someone appears calm and collected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' reads as calm, but means written as music: melodies are composed.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting on affected manner is a pretence of appearance, and melodies or tunes are pieces written by composers.

clue.text: Kind of bender the vanquished go on

definitions.meaning: the defeated sink down to kneel before the victor

explanation.surface: A drinking spree that losers embark on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bender' suggests a drinking bout; here it is something that bends. The defeated go down on bended joints.
explanation.definitionFit: This leg joint bends, and those who surrender traditionally kneel down on both.

parts.note: AC is alternating current
a tor is a rocky hill or outcrop, common on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A musician who plays in a contemporary rock band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current rock player' reads as a modern rock musician; the player is a stage performer.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage performer playing a role is a player in the old theatrical sense.

parts.note: an ass is a donkey, an animal

indicators.note: the letters of nest are built into a different structure

explanation.surface: A donkey consents to construct a nest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'building' rearranges NEST into ENTS, which follows ASS.
explanation.definitionFit: To consent or concur is to give approval, as in going along with a proposal.

parts.note: suggests the railway carriage used by the monarch, but means the people who follow a king or queen

explanation.surface: The special railway carriages used by the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'train' is the attendants following a dignitary, not a locomotive.
explanation.definitionFit: A body of attendants accompanying an important person forms their entourage or train.

clue.text: Needle for decoration on artificial silk

parts.note: the OBE is a British honour, the Order of the British Empire

indicators.note: artificial silk is not the real thing, so its letters are made up into another form

explanation.surface: A sewing needle is used to embroider artificial silk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'artificial' rearranges SILK to LISK, placed after OBE. Cleopatra's Needle in London is one such monument.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall tapering stone pillar is called a needle, as in Cleopatra's Needle.

indicators.note: silly or foolish, so the words sin seem are muddled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone seeking revenge makes wrongdoing look foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fatuous' rearranges SIN SEEM.
explanation.definitionFit: Retribution, named after the Greek goddess of divine punishment.

indicators.note: the name Teresa is broken up and its letters set in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A woman called Teresa gets a holiday break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break' looks like part of 'holiday break', but it rearranges TERESA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Christian festival of the Resurrection is marked by a spring public holiday.

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word the is used

parts.note: an issue of a newspaper or magazine is an edition

explanation.surface: Someone needs the first edition of a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the first' gives T, the first letter of 'the', followed by ISSUE. 'Paper' looks like a newspaper, but it is soft paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft thin paper, as in tissue paper or a paper handkerchief.

indicators.note: the letters are taken out of the run of words goods wagons

explanation.surface: Goods are stolen from railway freight wagons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' picks the letters out of goodS WAGons. The stray D in the printed clue is a misreading.
explanation.definitionFit: Loot or plunder taken by a thief is slang for stolen goods.

indicators.note: the letters of the other entry are to be altered into a fresh order

parts.note: the entry at 18 across, a leg joint

explanation.surface: Someone is anxious to alter a crossword entry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' rearranges the four letters of the 18-across entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Being enthusiastic or eager is wanting something very much.

clue.text: It's not often the present combines with the past

parts.note: now is the present time
and joins things, like with
then means at a time in the past

explanation.surface: Rarely does present-day life mix with history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'combines' is a link here, and 'with' gives AND, joining the two times.
explanation.definitionFit: Occasionally, from time to time, is the opposite of frequently.

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do
N is north, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A moment of contrasting highs and lows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High light' reads as a highlight; it is a light high in the sky. 'low' is the noise cattle make.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth's natural satellite shines high in the night sky.

parts.note: suggests a spectacular outfit, but means jewellery that makes impressions in wax

explanation.surface: A garment that would wow anyone who saw it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'impressive' means something that makes an impression, pressed into sealing wax.
explanation.definitionFit: A finger band bearing a seal is pressed into wax to stamp a crest.
